summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, diabetes, chronic venous insufficiency, and heart failure was admitted after sustaining a traumatic wound to her right lower leg from a fall at her rehabilitation facility. The wound was deep, involving muscle and fascia, and she was admitted to vascular surgery for management. Her admission was complicated by acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine, likely due to dehydration, and a multidrug-resistant E. coli urinary tract infection sensitive only to meropenem. She was hydrated, her oral diabetes medications were held initially, and IV meropenem was started. After 24 hours of compression, she underwent debridement and VAC placement. Her kidney function improved, diabetes medications were resumed, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. The wound developed healthy granulation tissue, and she was discharged to extended care with plans for readmission for skin grafting. She was stable, afebrile, and in good condition at discharge.
problems: Open wound of knee, leg [except thigh], and ankle, complicated
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
